Items.Authors: José Pinto-Muñoz, Mauricio G. Solar
Items.Title: Comparison of natural language models for searches in virtual observatories
Items.Abstract: This work presents the development and evaluation of a web platform called Virtual Observatory (VO) Artificial Intelligence Search, enabling natural language queries on the astronomical VOs using state-of-the-art LLMs. The architecture includes an interactive frontend, coordinating backend, database, search engine compatible with IVOA’s SIAP protocols (International Virtual Observatory Alliance, Simple Image Access Protocol), and two LLMs: GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1. The main goal was to compare their performance in retrieving astronomical images, assessing precision, response time, resource consumption, and sustainability. Twenty-one thematic queries per model were executed, measuring Recall@1, Recall@3, MRR, tokens, cost, and carbon footprint. DeepSeek-R1 achieved higher Recall@3 (86 % vs. 71 %), lower cost and environmental impact, while GPT-4o was faster and used fewer tokens. The evaluation shows distinct strengths enhancing semantic access to large astronomical datasets.

Items.Authors: Michael Gardiner, Dave Ashby, Chris Contaxis, Trupti Ranka, Tomas Krasuski, Gary Muller, Jose Soto, Neil Mills, Austin Everman, Maria Hernandez, Hector Swett, Barbara Fischer, John Ford, Tommy Salanski, David Zeller, Trevor Dugan
Items.Title: Experimental validation of a CO2 refrigerant-based thermal control system for the Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT) primary mirror (M1) segments
Items.Abstract: The Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT) employs seven 8.4 meter diameter borosilicate primary mirror segments whose optical performance depends on maintaining them at thermal equilibrium with ambient air during operations to minimize local seeing effects and prevent figure distortions caused by temperature gradients. To meet these requirements, a prototype thermal control system that uses subcritical CO2 (R744) refrigeration was developed and integrated into the Primary Mirror Subsystem (M1S) test mirror cell. Testing at the Richard F. Caris Mirror Lab evaluated thermal performance using optical feedback as part of the Optical Performance Risk Reduction (OPRR) program. This paper presents the key results of the system testing, including thermal performance behavior and observations related to thermal print-through, along with lessons learned that will inform the final M1S Thermal Control design.

Items.Authors: Monika G. Petr-Gotzens, Vincenzo Forchì, Andrea Mehner, Thomas Bierwirth, John Pritchard, Ahmed M. Khan, Kevin Knecht, Olivier Hainaut, Andre Graca
Items.Title: Supporting users in their observation preparation - the ESO ObsPrep tool
Items.Abstract: Ground based observatories are experiencing significant technological advances and telescopes are getting equipped with highly complex instruments to enable cutting-edge astronomical research. The increasing complexity of such instruments displays a challenge to their users when they want to plan and prepare specific observation programmes, that often request to define large amount of detailed instrument-specific information.  Therefore, at ESO we developed an Observation Preparation tool (in short ObsPrep tool), which provides a layer of abstraction over the instrument-specific technical details and tries to harmonize the users' experience when being faced with the preparation of observation blocks for different complex instruments. Here, we present the core functionalities of ObsPrep, as well as its special features and how the user interface integrates into ESO's generic phase2 observation preparation tool.

Items.Authors: Guido Agapito, Fabio Rossi, Alfio Puglisi
Items.Title: SynIM: a high-performance GPU-accelerated Python library for synthetic interaction and tomographic reconstruction matrices in next-generation adaptive optics
Items.Abstract: Next-generation AO systems for 8-40m telescopes (e.g., MAVIS, MORFEO) demand high calibration accuracy. Rising complexity makes experimental calibration challenging due to time constraints and vibrations, establishing Model-Based (synthetic) calibration as the standard.    We present SynIM, an open-source Python library for computing synthetic Interaction and Projection Matrices. SynIM leverages GPU acceleration (CuPy) for high-order systems. A key innovation is "intelligent workflow optimization," which minimizes interpolation errors during geometric projection.    SynIM supports SCAO, MCAO, and LTAO configurations. It includes modules for atmospheric covariance and tomographic projection matrices, enabling MMSE reconstructor generation. Native support for legacy PASSATA (.pro) and modern SPECULA (.yaml) configurations ensures versatility. Combined with optimized multi-WFS computation, SynIM is a powerful tool for design simulations and operational calibration.

Items.Authors: Felix M. Thiel, Mayukh Bagchi, Laura M. Fissel, Aarchi Shah, Lindy Blackburn, Emily Butler, Rafael Costa, Thomas Emo, Vincent L. Fish, Daryl Haggard, Michael D. Johnson, Jess Lo, Maggie Oxford, Dominic W. Pesce, Ganesh Rajagopalan, Javier L. Romualdez, Adrian K. Sinclair, Bonnie Slocombe, Stephanie St-Jean, Terry Yang
Items.Title: The balloon‑borne VLBI experiment (BVEX) radio telescope and position tracking system
Items.Abstract: In this paper we present the design of a 22 GHz Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) station that launched from Timmins, Ontario, Canada in August 2025. We further present a sub-mm precision position tracking system built from commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) components used for phase-reconstruction. Though the previous BVEX flight was not successful due to issues with the balloon, there are plans to upgrade the telescope for a second flight from Palmas, Tocantins, Brazil in 2027.

Items.Authors: Lina Gatilova, Jean-Baptiste Cuvellier, Thibaut Vacelet, Antonella Cavanna, Yong Jin, Jeanne Treuttel
Items.Title: 2THz GaAs MMIC mixer for astronomy applications
Items.Abstract: Space-based observations at terahertz frequencies provide access to key spectral lines that are essential for studying chemical composition and atmospheric dynamics. Among these, the ionized oxygen transition near 2.06 THz is of particular interest, as it enables the retrieval of wind velocities in the Earth's upper atmosphere using a compact heterodyne receiver. Schottky-diode-based heterodyne receivers remain one of the best solutions for detecting molecular spectra in millimetre and submillimetre wave range. Our current work focus on extending of GaAs MMIC Schottky-diode technology toward operation up to 5 THz frequencies. In this contribution we will present the development of new 2 THz (1960-2120 GHz) sub-harmonic mixer. The design, the MMIC topology optimization, fabrication process and first DC measurements are discussed.

Items.Authors: Lorenzo Natalucci, Philippe Laurent, Marica Branchesi, Mariateresa Fiocchi, Lorraine Hanlon, Miguel Mas-Hesse, Aline Meuris, Paul O'Brien, James C. Rodi, Simone Scaringi, Konrad R. Skup, Norbert Werner, Silvia Zane, Julia Alfonso-Garzon, Biswajit Banerjee, Patrizia Barria, Anthony J. Bird, Soren Brandt, Gabriele Bruni, Floriane Cangemi, Gianluca Castignani, Eric Chassande-Mottin, Sylvain Chaty, Jerome Chenevez, Alexis Coleiro, Francesco Dazzi, Alessio L. De Santis, Phil Evans, Olivier Godet, Diego Gotz, Rene Hudec, Lucien Kuiper, Angela Malizia, Sheila McBreen, Sandro Mereghetti, Manuela Molina, Filip Munz, David Murphy, Gor Oganesyan, Francesca Panessa, Elena Pian, Jakub Ripa, Oliver J. Roberts, Samuele Ronchini, Fabian Schussler, Vojtěch Šimon, Nial Tanvir, Alexey Uliyanov, Nello Vertolli, Stanislav Vìtek, Ugo Zannoni
Items.Title: GRINTA: a new probe of the dynamic universe
Items.Abstract: Recent observations of the transient sky at all wavelengths are increasingly revealing the importance of the multi-messenger and multi-wavelength approach. The GRINTA (Gamma-Ray INternational Tran-  sient Array Observatory) satellite, proposed for launch around the middle of the next decade, is conceived as a small mission with good sensitivity, excellent angular resolution and fast follow-up capability for studying transient sources at timescales from ms to hours, at the same time ensuring optimal integration with multi-messenger networks. The GRINTA mission will carry two complementary payloads to cover in total the 5-10,000 keV band, that will detect and localize gamma-ray bursts covering ~ half the sky and will be able to perform imaging surveys with sub-arcmin resolution. GRINTA will operate in synergy with the most powerful electromagnetic, gravitational wave and neutrino observatories foreseen to be operational after~2035.

Items.Authors: Jérôme Amiaux, Fabien Malbet, Florence Ardellier-Desages, Eduardo Bendek, Eric Doumayrou, Pierre-Antoine Frugier, Renaud Goullioud, Thomas Greene, Pierre-Olivier Lagage, Manon Lizzana, Jerome Martignac, Julien Michelot, Fabrice Pancher, Thibault Pichon, Aki Roberge, Samuel Ronayette, Hugo Rousset, Breann Sitarski
Items.Title: High-precision high-accuracy astrometry for the Habitable World Observatory
Items.Abstract: We present a comprehensive system analysis for an instrument onboard the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), designed for high-precision, high-accuracy differential astrometry. The analysis integrates the definition of the mission profile, the instrumental concept architecture, and an error budget that breaks down the key contributors to the sub-µas precision required for a single measurement. The proposed architecture of the instrument concept is derived from error budget and mission constraints based on a large visible detector array composed of an assembly of multiple CMOS sensor chips resulting in an overall gigapixel focal plane, with a technological maturation plan leading to TRL 5 for the Mission Consolidation review in 2029.

Items.Authors: Richard Lord, Caroline Jaillot, Kaila Hall-Smith, Lucio Tirone, Oscar Moyo, Luca Stringhetti
Items.Title: Planning and executing the verification of the SKAO radio telescopes
Items.Abstract: The world’s largest two Radio Telescopes are currently in the middle of their construction lifecycles: 1. The SKA-Low  Radio Telescope is currently being constructed in Western Australia's Murchison shire on the traditional lands of the  Wajarri Yamaji. The full design baseline will consist of 131,072 antennas and will operate in the “Low” 50 MHz –  350 MHz frequency range. 2. The SKA-Mid Radio Telescope is currently being constructed in South Africa’s Karoo  region. The full design baseline will consist of 197 steerable dishes, which includes the 64 dishes of the MeerKAT Radio  Telescope, and will operate in the “Mid” 350 MHz – 15.4 GHz frequency range.  This paper describes the process that is being followed to plan and execute the verification of these Radio Telescopes  against their requirements. The scale and multi-national nature of this project brings many challenges, and the objective of this paper is to share how these challenges are being addressed.

Items.Authors: Chandan Bhat, John Young, David Buscher, Christopher A. Haniff, Fabien R. Baron
Items.Title: Variational inference-based polychromatic imaging for optical interferometry
Items.Abstract: We present a variational inference–based optical interferometric imaging method using a compactness-enforcing prior model. The prior helps to model disks, Gaussians, rings, and supports resolving the central compact component in young stellar objects. It combines a limb-darkened compactness weight, harmonic-smoothed log-intensity field, and a polychromatic formulation that reconstructs all wavelengths simultaneously. Implemented in NIFTy with MGVI, the method is validated on simulated data and applied to beta Lyrae, HD 190073, and also recovers sparse fields of point-like sources from the 2016 Interferometric Imaging Beauty Contest dataset.

Items.Authors: Jorge Fuentes-Fernández, Jaime Ruíz-Díaz-Soto, José Leonardo Garcés Medina, Fernando Ángeles Uribe, Alejandro Farah Simon, Sebastián F. Sánchez
Items.Title: ÉBANO: an angular-scanning integral field spectrograph
Items.Abstract: ÉBANO is a low-cost integral-field spectrograph with a wide field of view of 6.5 arcmin squared, installed on the 84-cm telescope at the Mexican National Astronomical Observatory in Sierra de San Pedro Mártir. The wavelength scan is done by tilting a narrowband filter, hence shifting the transmitted light to shorter wavelengths. The instrument has two filters which cover spectral lines of [OIII] and Hb with a spectral resolution of R~330, and [SII], HeI, Ha and [NII] with R~500. All the optomechanics have been done by additive manufacturing (3D printing), showing an excellent performance. We have developed a liquid cooling system for the CCD. The first observational campaign of ÉBANO will be a complete cartography of the Andromeda galaxy with a spatial resolution never achieved before. We present an overview of the instrument, laboratory performance and commissioning at the telescope.

Items.Authors: Jalo Nousiainen, Markus Kasper, Vincent Chambouleyron, Benoit Neichel, Iremsu Taskin, Olivier Absil, Gilles Orban De Xivry, Sylvain Cetre, Jean-François Sauvage, Florian Ferreira, Markus Bonse, Byron Engler
Items.Title: Reinforcement learning for wavefront control: from WFS control to focal plane and from numerical simulations to lab and on-sky
Items.Abstract: Achieving high-contrast imaging with ELT-PCS requires a fast, robust control system. Detecting nearby Exo-Earths demands high contrast at separations of only tens of milliarcseconds, where performance is limited by fast-varying XAO residuals and quasi-static speckles. Reinforcement Learning (RL) is an emerging solution that has been shown to mitigate temporal and misregistration errors and to adapt to moderately non-linear wavefront sensing. Remaining challenges include on-sky validation, handling strongly non-linear sensors, and focal-plane control for quasi-static speckles. We present advances on all fronts: first on-sky tests on PAPYRUS at OHP, a new low-latency TensorRT implementation, and prospects for SCExAO; a new end-to-end RL algorithm combining reconstruction and control to extend ZWFS dynamic range on GHOST; and mode-based RL focal-plane control using sequential phase diversity for dynamic and static NCPA correction without prior optical models.

Items.Authors: N. A. Levenson, M. López-Morales, I. N. Reid
Items.Title: Community programs to observe targets of opportunity
Items.Abstract: Variable and transient phenomena are astrophysically revealing, exhibiting extreme energetics or unusual states. They are broadly described as “targets of opportunity” (ToOs) because the observing target is not defined in advance. A wide scientific community has interest in obtaining time-sensitive, multi-wavelength observations of some rare transient objects. The events’ rare nature demands observatory support of long-term programs. Observing configurations should reflect broad community interest, and data should be widely available promptly.    We are developing Community ToO Programs for observations using the Hubble Space Telescope and the James Webb Space Telescope, with input from the astronomical community. We are pursuing four categories of programs, and we will work with experts beyond STScI to develop the them, including setting triggering criteria, observing modes, and cadence. The data collected under these programs will be immediately available to the science community.

Items.Authors: Jiaben Lin, Liyue Tong, Mingfu Shao, Hui Wang, Chen Yang
Items.Title: Explore the potential of large language models in astronomy: a pilot application framework implemented in solar physics
Items.Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing the landscape of scientific research. Large Language Models (LLMs), as a cutting-edge technology of AI, is applied in diverse disciplines, enabling tasks ranging from literature reading, summarization and programming. Here, we present an application framework for implementing AI4S (Artificial Intelligence for Science) leveraging LLMs, which has been successfully applied in solar physics and named JinWu. JinWu has successfully accomplished both scientific tasks and Agent tasks. Notably, in the challenging flare forecasting scientific task, JinWu demonstrates remarkable proficiency (true positive rate (TPR = 1.00), True Skill Statistic (TSS = 0.95)), highlighting the potential of LLMs in advancing scientific research. In this presentation, we will introduce the technical roadmap for the implementation of JinWu and share the recent test results.

Items.Authors: Alexander Díaz, Gaizka Murga, Santiago Royo, Maialen González, Noel Rodrigo, Jon Blanco, Jon Ander Paniagua, Joseba Blázquez, Andreas Förster, Sebastian Schmid, Philippe Gitton, Samuel Lévêque, Martin Dimmler
Items.Title: Final integration and testing for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) M1 Local Coherencer
Items.Abstract: The 39m primary mirror of the ELT is composed of 798 hexagonal segments. These are regularly replaced for recoating and have to be phased again. The Local Coherencer is a non-contact metrology system aimed to assist in the phasing of a target segment. The system simultaneously measures the relative pistons on the six sides of this segment with respect to neighbouring ones with an accuracy below 300nm (2 sigma) in a range of ±0.25mm using a patented partially coherent light interferometer.    The system has been produced, integrated, and thoroughly tested to demonstrate performance, even under different environmental conditions such as, gravity orientation, operational temperatures and external lighting conditions. To comply with performance requirements mathematical compensation models have been developed for some effects, such as temperature, gravity orientation and repeatable non-linearities.    This paper presents the final integration of the system and the acceptance testing results.

Items.Authors: Ref Bari, Graham Neely, Lucas Anderson, Sharanya Palit, Amelia Frickey, Kaylee DeGennaro, Sebastian Abreu, Noah Barton
Items.Title: Resolving Sgr A* at 86 GHz using T-REX: Time-Resolving Explorer Satellite
Items.Abstract: We present T-REX: The Time-Resolving Explorer Satellite, a mission concept for a low-Earth-orbit (LEO) small satellite (M~85kg, P~1kW, >$50M) designed to explore the feasibility of millimeter-wave very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) from space. T-REX will operate at 86 GHz and seeks to achieve a temporal resolution of 22.5 minutes, enabling minute-scale sampling of the light curves of Sgr A* and M87. By co-observing with ground radio telescopes, T-REX also seeks to time-resolve the accretion flow of Sgr A*, which varies on the timescale of minutes. By advancing the technology readiness of mm-wave receivers and compact antenna systems, T-REX will serve as a pathfinder for future space VLBI missions. We invite collaborators, particularly researchers with VLBI/radio instrumentation experience, to contribute to the maturation of this concept.

Items.Authors: Adam Densmore, Nianhua Jiang, Dominic Garcia, Deisy Formiga Mamedes, Lewis B. G. Knee, Jijun Xu, Po Tseng, Susan Song, Huifang Gu, Panna Patel, Justin Miller
Items.Title: Development and manufacturing of cryogenic low-noise amplifiers for SKA-Mid band 2 receivers
Items.Abstract: The Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre of the National Research Council Canada (NRC) is supplying the cryogenic low noise amplifiers (LNAs) for the Square Kilometer Array (SKA-Mid) Band 2 receivers. These amplifiers achieve ultralow average noise temperatures of ~1.3 K, flat gain profiles above 38 dB, low input and output return loss below -10 dB and demonstrate high gain stability. The LNAs were developed at NRC and their volume production is being performed by Nanowave Technologies Inc. In this paper, we describe the amplifier development, manufacturing process, performance variation observed across production batches and challenges faced in meeting SKAO’s stringent requirements.

Items.Authors: Julia Saleh Natur, Ehud Behar, Shlomit Tarem, Zvika Tarem, Omer Reich, Alex Vdovin, Amir Feigenboim, Solomon Margolin, Roey Evental
Items.Title: GALI localization of off-grid GRB directions: a comparison of rectangular and triangular calibration meshes
Items.Abstract: GALI (GAmma-ray burst Localizing Instrument) is a compact γ-ray burst (GRB) localization concept that determines source directions using directional count-rate modulations produced by internal shadowing within a 3D scintillator array. This work compares rectangular and triangular calibration meshes for off-grid GRB localization. Laboratory measurements with the full-scale detector demonstrate average localization accuracies of 0.86°±0.14° and 1.19°±0.28° for the triangular and rectangular meshes, respectively. Monte Carlo simulations of 50,000 GRBs under realistic Low Earth Orbit background conditions reproduce the same trend, yielding 1.91°±1.20° and 2.73°±2.18°, respectively. These results establish the triangular calibration mesh as the preferred calibration strategy for GALI. Additional simulations show sensitivity from 10 keV to ~1 MeV, with a peak effective area of ~130 cm² near 100 - 150 keV, and demonstrate degree-scale localization for compact CubeSat implementations.

Items.Authors: Rohan Gupta, John Monnier, Joel S. Bermudez, Fabien Baron
Items.Title: Revealing time-variable protoplanetary disk substructures via generative prior image reconstruction of optical interferometric data
Items.Abstract: Optical/infrared long-baseline interferometers such as VLTI and CHARA resolve sub-AU structure in protoplanetary disks, but reconstruction is ill-posed due to sparse Fourier coverage. This motivates the use of priors, which have traditionally been simple analytical regularizers. Generative neural networks such as normalizing flows or latent-diffusion models provide a more expressive prior class. We train a model on physically plausible disk morphologies and use it to regularize image reconstruction. For multi-epoch data, we apply a shared prior and combine likelihood terms to more robustly recover temporal variability. We will benchmark performance on archival datasets and compare with SQUEEZE and MiRA. Early tests show reduced artifacts and improved recovery of brightness asymmetries, with planned applications to new CHARA/VLTI observations.

Items.Authors: Florence Ardellier-Desages, Jérôme Amiaux, Eric Doumayrou, Pierre-Antoine Frugier, Pierre-Olivier Lagage, Jérôme Martignac, Thibault Pichon, Samuel Ronayette, Fabien Malbet, Fabrice Pancher, Manon Lizzana, Hugo Rousset, Julien Michelot
Items.Title: Technological maturation of a CMOS gigapixels astrometry instrument for Habitable World Observatory space mission
Items.Abstract: To meet its demanding the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) astrometric goals, a dedicated high-precision instrument is being developed around a gigapixel-class focal plane using Pyxalis’s new 220-MP GigaPyx CMOS sensors and an integrated calibration system. The project addresses three main challenges: validating detector performance, developing space-qualified packaging for a multi-sensor focal plane, and implementing on-board processing capable of reducing data volume by a factor of ~100. The maturation plan includes building a complete end-to-end detection chain to reach TRL 5 by the end of the program for the Mission Consolidation review in 2029.

Items.Authors: Allar Saviauk, Joar G. Brynnel, Christine Füßlein, Diana Johl, Mark Cunningham, Roelof S. de Jong, Steffen Frey, Olga Bellido-Tirado
Items.Title: The backbone of success: detailing the planning and execution of the 4MOST installation on VISTA telescope
Items.Abstract: Rigorous planning and preparation are crucial for the complex Assembly, Integration, and Verification (AIV) phases of large astronomical projects. The 4MOST Multi-Object Spectroscopic facility, comprising more than ten major subsystems, was successfully installed on ESO's VISTA telescope in October 2025 with zero schedule delays. This paper outlines the planning strategies and documentation that ensured timely completion, describes the stepwise integration process, and highlights the use of tailored digital tools such as Jira for progress tracking and test reporting. We conclude with lessons learned and recommendations to further optimize AIV for future large-scale astronomical instruments.

Items.Authors: Haosheng Lin
Items.Title: Flare Sentinel: a compact integral field spectrograph for the observation of the Balmer series spectra during solar flare
Items.Abstract: Flare Sentinel is a compact integral field spectrograph (IFS) dedicated to the observation of the hydrogen Balmer series spectral lines during flares at the Haleakala Observatory on Maui, Hawaii. It consists of a 200 mm aperture telescope and a 96 x 50 pixel format integral field unit (IFU) with a 1’’/pixel spatial sampling size, followed by a compact spectrograph array consisting of 96 miniature spectrographs with 0.2 nm spectral resolution. The 350 – 450 nm spectral window covers the Balmer break at 364 nm to the H_gamma line at 463 nm. Flare Sentinel is fabricated using an ultra-precision free-form micro optics fabrication technology developed by Canon Inc. of Japan. This technology can fabricate monolithic image slicer with 0.03 mm slicer mirrors with multiple ridges and valleys. Construction of Flare Sentinel completed in October 2025. This paper will present the mechanical and optical design of Flare Sentinel IFS, laboratory performance test results, and on-sun data.

Items.Authors: Eric Villard
Items.Title: The Space Array initiative and SHARP precursor mission
Items.Abstract: Ground-based astronomy has progressed through better sites and larger telescopes like VLT, ALMA, and soon SKA and ELT, but rising complexity and atmospheric conditions worsening with frequency highlight the need to move high-resolution astronomy into space. Interferometry is the only route to resolutions beyond single-dish limits, yet past space VLBI missions with a single antenna were constrained by limited baseline distribution. True breakthroughs require a multi-satellite array. SHARP, a mission concept, proposed three sub-mm satellites to demonstrate key technologies and enable event-horizon-scale imaging. Looking ahead, the Space Array envisions tens of antennas in Earth’s orbit for transformative resolution and imaging. We outline both initiatives and argue that scientific demand and technological readiness make this the right moment for space-based interferometric arrays.

Items.Authors: Jonathan W. Arenberg
Items.Title: Architecting the Habitable Worlds Observatory for the 21st century
Items.Abstract: The field of space technology is rapidly changing as we enter the second quarter of the 21st century and enter the pre-formulation period for Habitable Worlds Observer (HWO). This rapid advancement in technologies and operating concepts can even be considered a revolution in our field. We will introduce the idea that this revolution also impacts considerations in the mission architecture of the HWO. The three space ages are defined along with their design paradigms and ethos. The challenge of designing a flagship mission such as HWO as a mission of the current space age is presented and we will show that some of the elements of the new space revolution can relax some of these constraints. Inclusion of these new technologies and concepts is not free, and we will examine how architecting for the new space age is different than for previous missions.

Items.Authors: Mark H. Cunningham, Olga Bellido-Tirado, Roelof S. de Jong, Joar G. Brynnel, Steffen Frey, Genoveva Micheva, Roland Winkler, Weijia Sun, Allar Saviauk, Domenico Giannone, Andreas kelz, Isobel Hook, Jonathan irwin, Mike Irwin, Arto Jarvinen, Jens-Kristian Krogager, Johan Richard, Jake Laas, Jonathan Loveday, Hugo Mendez-Hernandez, Ignacio Del Moral Castro, Daniel Sablowski
Items.Title: System Verification of 4MOST: planning, execution, and lessons learned
Items.Abstract: 4MOST is a new wide-field, fibre-fed spectroscopic survey facility for ESO’s VISTA telescope, delivering 2436 simultaneous spectra over a 4.2 deg² field of view through a tilting-spine fibre positioner and three dedicated spectrographs. Following integration and verification in Europe, the full system has now been successfully verified and commissioned at Paranal, achieving first light in October 2025. This paper outlines the verification methodology and key results from both pre-shipment and on-site campaigns, assessing performance in areas such as throughput, image quality, fibre positioning accuracy, spectral resolution, stability, and operational reliability. The findings confirm that 4MOST meets its scientific and technical requirements and is now fully operational as an ESO facility instrument. Lessons learned from the European and Chilean campaigns are discussed with a view to improving verification workflows for future large-scale spectroscopic instruments.

Items.Authors: Kayla Spencer, Massimiliano Galeazzi, Russell Roberts, Madison Pacheco, Frederick S. Porter, Kip Kuntz, Rousseau Nutter, Nicholas E. Thomas, Gabriel Loftus, David Sibeck, Brian Walsh, Jason Swasey, Takashi Okajima
Items.Title: The lobster eye x-ray telescope
Items.Abstract: The Lobster Eye X-ray Telescope (LXT) utilizes micropore (lobster eye) optics to address a key limitation in current X-ray instrumentation for a wide field of view. When coupled with large-area CCD detectors, the instrument achieves good angular resolution and energy resolution across a broad energy range. The short focal length of these optics results in a lightweight telescope with a low moment of inertia, a design that enables rapid repointing. LXT's primary mission focuses on observing extended diffuse emissions from sources like the Local Hot Bubble, the Galactic Halo, and the Cygnus Loop, all while mitigating foreground contamination from Solar Wind Charge Exchange (SWCX).

Items.Authors: Joshua Montgomery, Graeme Smecher, Maclean Rouble, Ketan Sand
Items.Title: 100GbE data acquisition and online triggering for KID pulse detection at µs timescale
Items.Abstract: Applications that deploy Kinetic Inductance Detector (KID) arrays for pulse detection, such as for particle-physics and photon-counting, often require >1 MHz of readout bandwidth to recover pulse shapes and arrival times. Multiplexed arrays require enormous data throughput, so pulse triggers are typically implemented in firmware onboard the readout. These triggers are resource intensive and have limited functionality. We introduce a client-side triggering architecture that addresses these limitations using the 1/10/25/100 GbE networking throughput of the Radio Frequency System on a Chip (RFSoC)-based t0.CRS system. We demonstrate real-time pulse detection and capture with 2.44 MHz of complex bandwidth while maintaining visibility into the full-rate data. The online trigger includes dynamic thresholding, multi-sample coincidence logic, and 1 GbE and 100 GbE offload data paths.

Items.Authors: Stanimir O. Letchev, Julian Stürmer, Jacob Pember, Matheus J. Castro, Vincent Benz, Christian Schwab, Lars A. Buchhave, Ansgar Reiners, Sebastian Schäfer
Items.Title: 2ES: design and development of the calibration system
Items.Abstract: The Second-Earth Spectrograph (2ES) is a planned fiber-fed, high-resolution echelle spectrograph for the 2.2m ESO/MPG telescope in La Silla, Chile. Its intended goal is to detect Earth-mass planetary candidates around solar-type stars, which will require a radial-velocity (RV) precision of ~10cm/s. In order to achieve this precision, 2ES will observe the same bright targets for 5 years with a spectral resolution of 120,000 over the wavelength range of 370 nm to 850 nm. Maintaining a stable calibration at the level of 10 cm/s for 5 years is an extreme engineering challenge. In this submission, we present the overall design of the 2ES calibration system and the strategies we intend to employ to reach the scientific goals of the project.

Items.Authors: Jacob Pember, Julian Stürmer, Matheus J. Castro, Stanimir Letchev, Vincent Benz, Christian Schwab, Lars A. Buchhave
Items.Title: 2ES: design of the image slicer and double scrambler
Items.Abstract: The Second Earth Spectrograph (2ES) is a next-generation extreme precision radial velocity spectrograph with the goal of discovering terrestrial planets in the habitable zone around the brightest solar-type stars in the sky. An integral part of this system is the fibre link, the implementation of which can have a significant impact on the stability of the spectrograph illumination, critical to achieving the instrument's ambitious scientific goals. This fibre link will include an image slicer, with light from an octagonal fibre from the telescope spatially remapped onto a rectangular fibre to the spectrograph. This image slicer will also act as a double scrambler, in which the far-field from one fibre is imaged onto the near-field of the other. In this proceeding, we discuss the requirements of the slicer/scrambler system within the wider context of the 2ES project and outline our current ideas for its design.

Items.Authors: Julian Stürmer, Santiago Barboza, Rafael Brahm, Lars A. Buchhave, Matheus de Jesus Castro, Guillermo B. Guinea, Thomas Henning, Niels C. Jessen, Andres Jordan, Heidi H. Korhonen, Laura Kreidberg, Ralf Launhardt, Stanimir O. Letchev, Jacob Pember, Andreas Quirrenbach, Ansgar Reiners, Ralf-Rainer Rohloff, Sebastian Schäfer, Christian Schwab, Andreas Seifahrt, Trifon Trifonov, Andrew Vanderburg, Mathias Zechmeister, Jinglin Zhao, Vincent Benz, Tobias Schmidt
Items.Title: 2ES: updates on the 2nd earth spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The discovery of true Earth analogues is a key goal in exoplanetary science, with implications for our understanding of planetary formation and the potential for life beyond our solar system. The 2nd Earth Spectrograph (2ES) initiative is an upcoming extreme-precision radial velocity (EPRV) instrument designed to observe a select sample of about 30 solar-like stars with high cadence over a period of >5 years, using the 2.2m ESO/MPG telescope in Chile. 2ES is a fiber-coupled instrument covering a wavelength range of ~370-850nm with a resolving power of 120000, making it an ideal tool for detecting the tiny Doppler shifts induced by Earth-mass planets. Here, we report on the current status of the design, including the performance of the procured optics and the results of our prototype testing. We also discuss the remaining technical challenges that must be addressed to achieve the required radial velocity precision.

Items.Authors: Wouter M. Laauwen, Jose R. Silva, Matvey Finkel, Stephen Yates, Behnam Mirzaei, Abram Young, Craig Kulesa, Chris Walker, Jian-Rong Gao
Items.Title: 4.7 THz local oscillator system with beam multiplexing for GUSTO
Items.Abstract: We present the as-built design and analysis of a 4.7 THz local oscillator (LO) system with beam multiplexing. The LO system, based essentially on a quantum cascade laser (QCL) source and a phase grating for multiplexing, provided eight LO signals for an eight-pixel hot electron bolometer (HEB) detector array operating in heterodyne mode. The system flew on the GUSTO stratospheric balloon mission during the 2023–24 Antarctic summer. We present the development approach from system requirements to the final design solution. A tolerance analysis is included to demonstrate compliance with system requirements. Finally, we present the functionality and performance of the key elements of the LO system.

Items.Authors: Andreas Kelz, Allar Saviauk, Thomas Jahn, Dennis Plüschke, Walter Seifert, Florence Laurent, Jean-Emmanuel Migniau, Peter Weilbacher, Johan Richard
Items.Title: 4MOST fiber system: integration, verification, and commissioning
Items.Abstract: 4MOST is a multi-object spectroscopic survey facility for the VISTA telescope with a large multiplex achieved by over 2400 optical fibers. The entire instrument has been installed and commissioned at ESO’s Paranal observatory in 2025.   This poster presents the complex installation of the 27m long science fibers from the positioner at the focal plane, through the Cassegrain Cable Wrap, to the high and the two low-resolution spectrographs below the Azimuth floor. In addition, various auxiliary fiber systems were installed and verified, which include simultaneous calibration fibres, mini-fiber-bundles for acquisition and guiding, fiducial fibers for reference, and a back-illumination of all fibers for metrology purpose. We show the on-sky performance of the fiber system based on the commissioning results, which feature 812 spectra for each spectrograph.

Items.Authors: M. C. Diez-González, I. López-Fernández, I. Malo-Gómez, R. I. Amils Samalot, A. García-Merino, J. D. Gallego Puyol
Items.Title: A 10k 31-50GHz cryogenic low-noise amplifier with thin-barrier InP pHEMTs for radio astronomy front ends
Items.Abstract: We present the design, fabrication, and cryogenic characterization of a prototype improved low-noise cryogenic amplifier developed for the 31–50 GHz Q-band receiver at Yebes Observatory. The four-stage hybrid amplifier features 2-finger × 25 µm gate width and 100 nm gate length pHEMTs, with a newly improved thin-Schottky-barrier first-stage transistor. Custom laser-milled matching networks and a compact gold-plated housing ensure robust thermal and RF integration. The RF interfaces support both 2.4 mm coaxial connectors and WR-22 waveguides, the latter providing lower loss and direct compatibility with the receiver front end. To accurately measure its extremely low noise temperature, a dedicated cryogenic waveguide variable-temperature load was developed. Measurements at 6 K demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, with an average noise temperature of 10 K and gain exceeding 35 dB, supporting the receiver’s role in detecting new molecular species in the interstellar medium.

Items.Authors: Zhen Zhang, Guifeng Chen, Yonggang Gu, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: A 3D measurement method for fiber-array end faces based on fringe projection
Items.Abstract: The defocus of fiber array endfaces affects the observational efficiency of spectroscopic telescopes. High-precision measurement of fibers embedded in micro-ceramic ferrules remains challenging due to their small size. This paper presents a binocular 3D measurement method based on fringe projection. Fringe patterns are projected to obtain phase information of fiber endfaces, and phase correspondence between stereo views is established via phase unwrapping for stable subpixel matching. Simulation results demonstrate that phase information can establish reliable stereo correspondences and achieve robust matching of fiber end faces, thereby verifying the feasibility of the proposed approach for subsequent three-dimensional reconstruction and defocus measurement.

Items.Authors: Tiago Giorgetti, Rodrigo L. Pereira, Laird M. Close, Jared R. Males, Hossein R. Najafabadi, Olivier Durney, Maggie Y. Kautz, Adam Fletcher, Claudia Mendes de Oliveira
Items.Title: A compact atmospheric dispersion corrector mechanism for GMT’s GMagAO-X exoplanet instrument
Items.Abstract: We present a compact Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector (ADC) for the GMagAO-X optical bench at the Giant Magellan Telescope. The mechanism is tailored to ELT-class ExAO constraints and fits within a densely populated, gravity-invariant floating table while minimizing vignetting. The design employs a large-diameter spur ring gear driven by a compact motor–gearhead–encoder stack; a front screw with a compression spring sets axial pinion–ring alignment during assembly. The ADC rotates a Zemax-derived triplet on a three-point edge support (no tip/tilt) and uses Hall-effect homing with a small magnet for repeatable absolute referencing. We summarize the architecture, bench interfaces, alignment approach, and integration outcomes, demonstrating ExAO-grade repeatability and low obscuration in a tightly constrained envelope.

Items.Authors: Tania Sofia Gomes Machado, Elisa Portaluri, Kalyan K. R. Santhakumari, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Alessandro Ballone, Federico Battaini, Maria Bergomi, Andrea Bianco, Simone Di Filippo, Marco Dima, Jacopo Farinato, Pierre Jouve, Michele Frangiamore, Davide Giughello, Davide Greggio, Dhiraj Gupta, Luigi Lessio, Demetrio Magrin, Luca Marafatto, Felipe Pedreros Bustos, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Valentina Viotto, Roberto Ragazzoni
Items.Title: A comparative study of strategies to replicate sodium LGS in a laboratory environment
Items.Abstract: The next generation of Adaptive Optics (AO) systems relies heavily on Laser Guide Stars (LGS) to expand sky coverage. Since LGS are extended objects, unlike Natural Guide Stars (NGS), dedicated AO technologies are required. Accurate testing of these new technologies on benches like MATTO and the Ingot WFS (I-WFS) requires high-fidelity laboratory replication of LGS properties, including variable profiles and geometry. We present a comparison of three distinct LGS-like source solutions tested on the I-WFS Bench: screens (OLED/LCD), fluorescent materials (Rhodamine-6G/Eosin Y) and holograms. By using the pupil uniformity of the I-WFS as a performance metric, we evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of each method to guide future laboratory test bench development.

Items.Authors: Jensen Hoy, Shana Sullivan, Vrinda Singhal, Tsz Chiu, Giorgio Savini, Thomas Schlichter
Items.Title: A COTS near-UV folded Czerny-Turner spectrometer and FlatSat for CubeSat OB-star monitoring
Items.Abstract: This work describes a compact near-UV Czerny–Turner spectrometer and flatsat demonstrator built entirely from commercial optics and opto-mechanics for future use on a 4U CubeSat. Starting from an existing astigmatism-free bicylinder design (Q. Zhou and Z. Zou, 2022), we re-optimise the spectrometer for the 300-330 nm OB-star band and convert the prescription into a manufacturable assembly using adjustable clamps and 3D-printed prototypes. A Raspberry-Pi-based flatsat stack then acquires spectra and runs a C pipeline that fits line centroids, widths, and fluxes for low-bit-rate downlink. We will present measured resolving power and throughput and discuss lessons for re-using optimised COTS spectrographs in UV small-satellite missions.

Items.Authors: Christian M. Pommranz, Konrad Dennerl, Emanuele Perinati, Michael J. Freyberg, Chris Tenzer, Andrea Santangelo
Items.Title: A digital twin of the eROSITA camera: readout modeling workflow for Monte Carlo simulations
Items.Abstract: As SRG/eROSITA is the first X-ray instrument at L2, the characterization of its instrumental background is of special importance. Previously, Geant4 simulations of the filter wheel closed background were conducted using a highly detailed mass model of the eROSITA camera. In this work, a readout modeling workflow was developed for post-processing of the Geant4 simulation results. This new workflow precisely models the entire readout procedure and produces FITS files that are compatible with the eROSITA Science Analysis Software System (eSASS), resulting in a digital twin of the eROSITA camera. This workflow has been shown to reproduce the drop at high energies above 9 keV observed in the measured filter wheel closed spectrum. Additionally, the workflow provides new insights by complementing the results of the previous Geant4 simulations with additional observables. Furthermore, the new workflow enables the use of identical data analysis for simulation and measurement data.

Items.Authors: Stephen J. C. Yates, Auke Veninga, Geert Keizer, Willem Jellema, Martin Eggens, Nick de Keijzer, Shahab O. Dabironezare, Jochem J. A. Baselmans, Lorenza Ferrari
Items.Title: A flexible full system far infra-red kinetic inductance detector test facility
Items.Abstract: We have developed an ultra-low background cryogenic test facility to support the future missions like PRIMA (satellite) and POEMM (balloon), enabling us to push the (detector) technological readiness. The system is equipped with cryogenic re-imaging optics and is initially designed to operate in either a 3-4 THz or 6-12 THz band, by choice of quasioptical filters. The unique property of the system is that it has two operation modes. The first allows direct wideband access to the lab environment with a power loading of ~25 fW/pixel, enabled with cryogenic Neural-Density filters of ~50dB attenuation. Alternatively, the cryostat window can be closed and a cryogenic blackbody placed in the pupil stop at 4K, which allows for absolute calibration at ultra-low loading. Using this system enables us to present the first beam patterns and spectral response of lens-coupled absorber KID arrays at 6-12 THz, with a good match to simulations.

Items.Authors: Jiahao Zhou, Wenfei Liu, Yingfu Wang, Mengmeng Qian, Haoyang Zhang, Xianke Song, Kai Yun, Hongzhuan Hu, Jianping Wang, Jiaru Chu, Ping Zhang, Zhigang Liu, Zengxiang Zhou
Items.Title: A Grid-Based Matching Algorithm for Back-Illuminated Spots Using the Distribution Pattern of Fiber Positioning Units on LAMOST
Items.Abstract: To achieve efficient closed-loop control of the 4,000 fiber positioning units in the LAMOST telescope, this work addresses the limitations of the conventional nearest-neighbor matching method in handling dense and occasionally anomalous fiber positions. We propose a novel gridded spot matching algorithm, which utilizes the inherent regularity of the fiber layout as prior knowledge. By constraining the matching search within localized grid cells, the algorithm transforms a global matching challenge into efficient local comparisons. Implementation in LAMOST's closed-loop system shows that this method significantly improves both the processing speed and the robustness of fiber position detection.

Items.Authors: Chelsea Adelman, Steph Sallum
Items.Title: A JWST kernel phase interferometry search for post main sequence planets
Items.Abstract: Most exoplanets orbit stars that will eventually become white dwarfs (WDs), yet knowledge of their post-main-sequence (post-MS) evolution is still unconstrained. While some post-MS exoplanets have been detected, a large sample of directly-imaged systems is needed to constrain their evolution mechanisms. The faintness of WDs, which prohibits adaptive optics correction for most targets, makes space-based imaging an attractive approach. However, detections on orbits where migrating post-MS exoplanets may reside remain technically challenging. Kernel phase interferometry (KPI) can access these separations by treating a conventional telescope as an interferometer in post-processing. This yields moderate contrast (well suited to detecting cold giant planets around faint WD hosts) within the diffraction limit. We present a KPI analysis of JWST imaging of a large sample of WDs. We constrain the occurrence rate of WD-orbiting planets and discuss the implications for post-MS exoplanet evolution.

Items.Authors: Ulf Seemann, Christian Fruck, Alexander Buron
Items.Title: A mid-IR Fabry-Perot Etalon calibrator for VLT/CRIRES+
Items.Abstract: We present a concept study for a novel Fabry-Perot Etalon (FP) calibration system covering the mid-IR range 2um - 5um (KLM bands) of ESO's high-resolution infrared spectrograph CRIRES+ at the VLT. The FP system is optimized to provide robust wavelength calibration in the KLM bands and means to calibrate the spectrograph's entrance slit curvature independent of nighttime and telescope time on sky, thereby enhancing the CRIRES+ calibration capabilities out to 5um. We derive the system requirements, discuss the challenges and feasibility associated in this wavelength regime, present a concept design and its implementation into CRIRES+, and evaluate the achievable performance.

Items.Authors: Lanqiang Zhang, Qianhan Zhou, Nanfei Yan, Shuai Zhang, Xuejun Rao, Jinsheng Yang, Changhui Rao
Items.Title: A monolithic upgrade of the NVST adaptive optics system for multimode and prominence observations
Items.Abstract: The adaptive optics (AO) system of the 1-m New Vacuum Solar Telescope has been comprehensively upgraded to improve system stability and to enable closed-loop AO correction for solar prominences. The previous AO system integrated AO, GLAO, and MCAO modes but suffered from a complex optical layout and thermal instability in the Coude room, leading to alignment sensitivity and performance degradation. To address these limitations and meet the requirements of prominence correction, the system has been completely redesigned into a compact, monolithic, single-platform configuration. A reconfigurable composite wavefront sensor supports AO, GLAO, and MCAO modes, while a dedicated chromospheric wavefront sensor enables closed-loop AO correction on solar prominences. This presentation focuses on the optical and opto-mechanical redesign of the system and its expected performance improvements. Commissioning is scheduled for May 2026, and initial high-resolution observations will be presented.

Items.Authors: Zhemin Cai, Jonathan Moller, Chris Coote, Jessica Zheng, Michael Goodwin, Dylan Simpfendorfer, Helen McGregor, Jon Lawrence, Scott Smedley, Rémi Giroud, Johan Richard, Florence Laurent, Alexandre Jeanneau
Items.Title: A multiphysics thermal-mechanical framework for BlueMUSE: IFU layout evaluation and thermal-enclosure performance assessment
Items.Abstract: The Multi Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE), a key instrument of the Very Large Telescope (VLT), has enabled significant astrophysical discoveries over nearly a decade of operation and provides an important reference for the development of BlueMUSE, a blue-optimised panoramic integral-field spectrograph for the VLT. Previous MUSE studies employed a two-stage ANSYS FEA model coupled with Zemax simulations to assess thermally induced displacements of key optical components and compare predicted trends with on-site measurements. Building on this foundation, the present study extends the analysis to BlueMUSE, focusing on structural layout optimisation and thermal-shield performance. Three IFU layout options are evaluated to minimise thermally induced displacement relative to the FSU and to identify the most suitable configuration for maintaining slicer alignment. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations are then used to assess whether a 60 mm Va-Q-vip thermal shield can maintain the

Items.Authors: Brianna Peck, Jessica R. Lu, Lianqi Wang, Noah Stiegler, Richard Dekany, Brooke DiGia, Antonin H. Bouchez, Mark R. Chun, Philip Hinz, Peter L. Wizinowich, Maxwell A. Millar-Blanchaer, Charles-Antoine Claveau
Items.Title: A Pathway Towards Visible-Light Adaptive Optics at the W. M. Keck Observatory
Items.Abstract: We present performance simulations that map a pathway toward diffraction-limited visible-light adaptive optics at the W. M. Keck Observatory. Using end-to-end modeling with the MAOS (Multi-threaded Adaptive Optics Simulator) package, we compare three system architectures: KAPA (current facility upgrades), STRATA (a next-generation single-conjugate facility-wide system), and KOLA (a proposed multi-conjugate system). Our results show how advances in laser power, wavefront sensing, and deformable mirror technology improve performance from on-axis correction (KAPA/STRATA) to wide-field correction (KOLA). These simulations provide a roadmap for the evolution of adaptive optics at Keck, bridging current capabilities to future wide-field, visible-light correction.

Items.Authors: Nicolas J. Flagey, Laurent Pueyo, Laura E. Coyle, Marcio Melendez, Randal Telfer, Tyler M. McCracken, Matt Lallo, Rémi Soummer, Leonid Pogorelyuk, Iva Laginja
Items.Title: A semi-analytical error budget for the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: In this paper we present a suite of representative top-level error budgets for the Habitable Worlds Observatory produced by the ULTRA-CT team. This error budget relates the contrast stability (key to exoplanet detection using differential imaging) to the wavefront variance at the entrance of the coronagraph instrument, integrated over a suite of past temporal scales.

Items.Authors: Xue Yang, Chen Zhang, Zhixing Ling, Yuan Liu, Weimin Yuan
Items.Title: A significant micrometeoroid impact damage event on the EP-WXT in September 2025
Items.Abstract: The Einsten Probe (EP) satellite has been in operaion for two years, during which time the Wide-field X-ray Telescope (WXT) on board has been experiencing micrometeoroid impact almost every month. In September 2025, one such events resulted in the simultaneous capture of impact traces by multiple detectors. This paper provides a detailed report on the pixel damage caused by this event, including a comprehensive overview of the time of occurrence, the distribution of detector position, the duration of impact, the extent of the damage, and the observed changes.

Items.Authors: Roser Juanola-Parramon, Christopher Stark, Amber Young, Paul Scowen
Items.Title: A standalone near-UV coronagraph for detecting atmospheric biosignatures with the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: The near-ultraviolet (NUV) band enables detection of key atmospheric species such as O₂ and O₃ through their strong absorption between 200–400 nm. To access these features, the Habitable Worlds Observatory would require a standalone NUV coronagraph. Although NUV coronagraphy is challenging, its role as a characterization instrument relaxes several design trades: the inner working angle need only match that of the visible coronagraph, and prior knowledge of planet locations allows non-circular dark zones that improve throughput.    We present a preliminary design for a dedicated NUV coronagraph informed by science requirements, expected exoplanet yields, and atmospheric retrieval needs. We outline the rationale for separating the NUV instrument from the main coronagraph, evaluate candidate coronagraph architectures, assess polarization aberrations, and discuss suitable UV detectors and wavefront-control approaches.

Items.Authors: Arika Egan, Richard Cartwright, Joseph Linden
Items.Title: A visible IFU for HWO: characterizing ocean world habitability inside and outside of the solar system
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), NASA’s next Astrophysics Flagship mission, will absolutely revolutionize astrophysics, and has the potential to conduct complementary planetary science. A prime opportunity to understand exo-ocean worlds and their habitability can be found in visible-wavelength spatially resolved spectroscopy of solar system bodies. In the case of Europa, there are several absorption and emission features spanning the optical bandpass that offer unprecedented insight into the moon’s surface features, plume activity, and exosphere. HWO's long operational lifespan enables long-term monitoring of transient phenomena like geyser eruptions and surface composition changes. Such observations will provide breakthrough progression toward understanding the extent of interior-surface material exchange, which is essential for determining if they harbor habitable environments. To this end, we present a preliminary visible wavelength integral field spectrograph for HWO.

Items.Authors: Ruoyu Zhou, Renbin Yan, Yutong Qiao, Chit-Ho Hui
Items.Title: A white-pupil echelle spectrograph design for high-resolution integral field spectroscopy: achieving near-peak blaze efficiency for key emission lines
Items.Abstract: We present a CMOS-optimized modular white-pupil echelle spectrograph design for high-resolution (R ~ 24300) integral-field spectroscopy of optical nebular emission. Proposed as an alternative design for surveys like AMASE, the instrument uses a 150 mm f/10 collimator and a 408-channel, 220 micron microlens-array pseudo-slit, yielding 17% higher etendue than current configurations. Its white-pupil layout decoupling the disperser enables interchangeable echelle configurations. The system features three camera channels (432-514, 514-606, 627-759 nm) covering critical gas diagnostics ([O III], [N II], [S II], and Balmer lines). This compact format preserves major optical diagnostics required for targeted nebular astrophysics and gas kinematics.
